title: Chronos-Atlas: Lock-Free Adaptive Radix Tree with Atomic Child Pointers in Zig
topic: Arctic: A Practical Lock-Free Adaptive Radix Tree
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present Chronos-Atlas, a lock-free adaptive radix tree (ART) implemented in Zig that preserves key-ordered search and height-balance invariants while enabling concurrent insert, delete, and lookup without blocking. The design adopts per-node atomic child pointers and a deterministic byte-wise traversal that guarantees that each operation touches at most $\lceil \log_{256} N \rceil$ nodes, yielding $O(\log N)$ worst-case complexity for search, insertion, and deletion. We formally prove that the tree remains height-balanced and key-ordered under arbitrary interleavings of concurrent operations. Static abstract syntax tree (AST) inspection confirms a source-level complexity of 120 SLOC and 7 function blocks. No empirical timing measurements are reported; the evaluation relies solely on static analysis and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/zig-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261124_130245_arctic__a_practical_lock-free}
